conviction_note: Near-balanced: the Q3 EPS bar ($2.31-2.33) sits inside a company guide set on 2026-09-08 with two months of the quarter known, and PM beat its own quarterly guides in Q1 and Q2 2026 (small positive), against a very hard US ZYN comparison (Q3 2025: 205m cans incl. promos, Nielsen offtake +39%) with BAT's Velo Plus taking share, a dollar that rose ~4% after the September guide (FY FX tailwind likely trimmed) and a +5.7% 20-day run-up to within 2% of the 52-week high; impact_sum -0.7 and the scaled -0.17 agree in sign, the scaled number is smaller because p_up was pulled to 48 for the pessimism artefact and because currency-only guide trims have been bought twice this year.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted diluted EPS: consensus $2.31 (Zacks, via https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3008728/philip-morris-q3-earnings-on-deck-key-factors-you-should-understand search snippet), $2.32 from 9 analysts (AAII, 2026-10-19, https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/517893-what-you-need-to-know-about-philip-morris-international-incs-q3-earnings; also Alphastreet $2.32 from 8 analysts), $2.33 (Earnings Whispers); revenue ~$11.38-11.42bn. Company guide for Q3 adjusted EPS $2.29-2.34 incl. +1c FX, raised 2026-09-08 from $2.20-2.25 (Barclays deck 8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001413329/000162828026060822/a2026barclays-slides.htm). FY2026 adjusted EPS guide $8.35-8.50 incl. +24c FX; ex-FX $8.11-8.26 (+7.5-9.5%). Q3 2025 adjusted EPS base $2.24. Bar is sourced (guide + agreeing estimates); consensus sits mid-to-upper of the guide.
positioning_check: Short interest 17.75m shares at 2026-09-30 settlement, ~1.1% of shares outstanding, 3.64 days to cover (up from 13.8m / 3.55 days at 09-15) per https://equibles.com/stocks/pm/short-interest — not crowded, no squeeze mechanism. Baseline: 25-delta skew +0.23 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.76, event-implied move 3.69% (straddle 4.18%), run-up +5.73% over 20d and +0.92% over 5d, -2.16% from 52w high, +39% from 52w low; AAII notes PM +3.5% since the Q2 print vs SPY +2.6%, forward P/E ~23.9.

findings.finding: PM raised its Q3 2026 adjusted EPS guide on 2026-09-08 (Barclays conference 8-K) to $2.29-2.34 including +1c FX, from $2.20-2.25 including -8c FX in July; consensus $2.31-2.33 sits in the mid/upper half, and PM beat its own prior quarterly guides this year (Q2 actual $2.20 vs guide $2.02-2.07; Q1 'exceeded our expectations'), so a small EPS beat vs the $2.32 bar is the base case — but the September guide was set with ~two-thirds of the quarter known and the dollar strengthened ~2-3% between Sep 8 and Sep 30 (roughly -1c of Q3 translation), so the beat is likely smaller than Q2's.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (guide $2.02-2.07, actual $2.20, FY held): +3.33%. Q1 2026 (adj EPS $1.96 +16%, 'exceeded expectations'): +6.98%. Q3 2025: -3.83% despite EPS beat (ZYN/smoke-free mix). EPS beats have been bought in 2026 but the reaction was driven jointly by ZYN offtake.
findings.why_not_priced: The guide and consensus are public, so the level is priced; what is not priced is the size of the habitual beat vs own guide. If the market expected a Q2-style 6-8% beat, consensus would sit at or above the $2.34 top of guide rather than at $2.31-2.33.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 beat vs own guide from the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001413329/000162828026049107/earningsreleasepm-ex991xq2.htm) and Q1 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001413329/000162828026026385/earningsreleasepm-ex991xq1.htm); Zacks trailing 4-quarter average surprise ~6%. FX drift from NAGA (https://naga.com/en/news-and-analysis/articles/forex-market-outlook). Lands inside the company guide.

findings.finding: The dollar index rose almost 4% from its 98.79 low on 2026-09-08 (the day PM set FY guidance at +24c FX 'at prevailing rates') to 102.54 on 2026-10-05, with EUR/USD down to ~1.116 after a Fed hike on 2026-09-16, so the FY2026 adjusted EPS guide of $8.35-8.50 is likely trimmed for currency on Oct 21 (rough estimate 5-8c, mostly Q4), the third FX-only revision of the year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 FY guide updated 'for currency only' with an impairment: stock +6.98%. Q2 2026 FY FX tailwind cut from +20c to +15c, ex-FX held: +3.33%. Currency-only cuts have been looked through twice in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: The dollar move is public and sell-side will have marked FX, so mostly priced; residual is whether management also signals Q4/2027 transactional pressure. If fully priced, FY consensus would already sit below the $8.35-8.50 guide midpoint (not verified; AAII shows 1 downward revision in the last month).
findings.independence: Barclays deck footnote for the +24c FX at Sep-8 rates (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001413329/000162828026060822/a2026barclays-slides.htm); EUR/USD 1.141 on July 22 from rate aggregator snippets. Macro-to-company transmission, a proxy: the company has not confirmed a new FX number.

findings.finding: US ZYN faces its hardest comparison of the year: Q3 2025 shipments were 205m cans (~3.08bn pouches, +37%) including a single-digit % of special promotional shipments, with Nielsen offtake +39% (September 2025 offtake reportedly +58%), while Q2 2026 offtake was only 'flat to slightly growing in a growing category' (2.9bn pouches) and BAT's US Modern Oral volume share rose 11.6 points to 29.8% in H1 2026 on Velo Plus; flat-to-down Q3 ZYN offtake and shipments near ~3.0-3.1bn are therefore likely, below thin Kalshi pricing that centred around 3.2-3.3bn, with 1.5mg/8mg dry launches and ZYN ULTRA (PMTA granted Aug 2026) as the offsets and a Q4 switch of 3mg/6mg dry cans to 20 pouches adding trade-inventory noise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2025 (ZYN shipments/revenue miss): -8.43%. Q1 2026 (shipments -23.5% but Nielsen offtake +10%): +6.98%. Q2 2026 (shipments +1.8%, offtake flat): +3.33%. The stock trades on ZYN offtake rather than shipments, in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: The yoy comparison is arithmetic on public numbers, and Seeking Alpha/Zacks previews flag 'tough ZYN shipment comparisons', so the direction is partly priced; what may not be is the size, since prediction-market pricing (Kalshi, thin, stale July snapshot) implied shipments above the 205m-can base. If fully priced, the stock would not be 2% off its 52-week high after a +5.7% 20-day run.
findings.independence: BAT H1 2026 report, US Modern Oral share 29.8% (+11.6pts), 2026-07-30 (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/british-american-tobacco--bats/half-year-report/9694649); PM Q2 2026 release on flat offtake (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001413329/000162828026049107/earningsreleasepm-ex991xq2.htm). Offtake for Q3 2026 is an inference: no scanner data for Jul-Oct 2026 was found. US ZYN is a single-digit share of group revenue; international smoke-free and combustible pricing (cig decline guided to only 2-3%) must hold for the group, which the September guide raise suggests they did.

findings.finding: IQOS stick prices in Japan rose on 2026-10-01 in the second step of the heated-tobacco excise reform (JT Ploom +¥40; PM applied 2026-07-27, and the Barclays deck says 'October pricing confirmed'), so Q3 Japan HTU shipments and IMS carry consumer and trade pantry loading, as Q1 did before the April step, when loading added ~4.5 points to Japan adjusted IMS growth (10.4% reported vs ~5.9% underlying).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026, the quarter with pre-April loading, HTU shipments +11.3%: stock +6.98%. Q2 2026, with pantry de-loading (Japan IMS -3.4%): +3.33%.
findings.why_not_priced: Almost certainly inside the Sep-8 Q3 guide, so it lands inside guidance; the residual is optics: a headline HTU growth figure flattered by loading, with a Q4 de-load that management will flag. If the market had marked it as a quality issue, the skew would lean to downside; it is balanced (+0.23).
findings.independence: Japanese price-change coverage (https://vegcale.com/2026/08/31/kanetsushiki-tabako-neage-2026-10/, https://www.kanaloco.jp/news/social/article-1307558.html) and the Barclays deck (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001413329/000162828026060822/a2026barclays-slides.htm). Shares no document with the EPS finding except the Barclays deck.

findings.finding: On 2026-09-18 PM raised its quarterly dividend 8.8% to $1.60 ($6.40 annualised), a larger step than any raise from 2019-2024, signalling board confidence in the cash flow outlook (operating cash flow guided ~$13.5bn).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print-day reaction history; dividend raises are announced separately in September.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is a month old and part of the run-up. Retained only as context that management did not hedge the outlook into the print.

findings.finding: PM goes into the print up 5.73% over 20 sessions and 2.2% below its 52-week high, at ~24x forward EPS (AAII) with short interest only ~1.1% of shares and 3.6 days to cover, so the bar for the reaction is higher than the EPS bar and there is no short base to squeeze on good news.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline's last seven reactions: 5 up, 2 down, median |move| 3.83%; the two down moves (Q2 2025 -8.43%, Q3 2025 -3.83%) came after strong rallies into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is itself the price; this finding says the run-up raises the bar, which the balanced skew does not offset.
findings.independence: AAII valuation and performance, 2026-10-19 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/517893-what-you-need-to-know-about-philip-morris-international-incs-q3-earnings); sealed baseline tape.

IQOS ILUMA US PMTA/MRTP still pending at FDA (filed Oct 2023, accepted Mar 2024); PM plans a scaled US IQOS launch only after authorisation and is spending H2 2026 to prepare it. No dated decision inside the window.

baseline_tension: Mostly agrees with the balanced skew: the evidence splits into a small positive on the EPS line (inside the company guide) and a small negative on ZYN and FX, against a +5.7% run-up that raises the reaction bar; nothing found cuts sharply against the option market.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Q3 EPS-beat finding moved from +0.5 to +0.3 because the bar sits inside a guide set on Sep 8 with most of the quarter known.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the Japan pantry-loading finding moved from +0.3 to +0.2, since it is almost certainly in the Q3 guide.

Rules 5 and 9 (proxy, segment net of the rest): the ZYN finding moved from -1.0 to -0.8, because Q3 2026 offtake is inferred from comparisons and BAT's share, not from a Q3 scanner number, and US ZYN is a single-digit share of group revenue.
Rule 1 (reaction history): the FX guide-trim finding moved from -0.4 to -0.3, because currency-only cuts were bought twice in 2026 (+6.98%, +3.33%).
Rule 7 (positioning): the run-up finding moved from -0.3 to -0.2 after confirming short interest is low (1.1%, 3.6 days) and the skew is balanced (+0.23).
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism': p_up moved from 47 to 48; understatement note: abs_move_pct moved from 4.2 to 4.3.
